title: AI Tutors Are Good at Answering. They're Bad at Holding Back.
summary: The Allen Institute for AI released TutorMoments, a study and public dataset that looks at the moments where a tutor has to choose between giving a student the answer and letting them struggle a little longer.

title: Memory Chips Are Sold Out Through 2027
summary: Reports say memory manufacturing capacity for 2027 has already been bought up, largely by AI data centre demand.

title: Oracle Bans AI-Generated Code From OpenJDK
summary: Oracle has barred AI-generated contributions from OpenJDK, the open-source project behind Java, which runs a large share of corporate software.

title: One Site Found 99% of Its Traffic Was Bots
summary: The owner of a 1.

title: The US Energy Department Launches Its Own Open AI Models
summary: The Department of Energy opened the Genesis Open Models Initiative, run out of Argonne National Laboratory, to build and publish AI models openly rather than behind a commercial licence.

title: Making Postgres 300x Faster at Analytics
summary: Engineers rebuilt the part of PostgreSQL that executes queries and reported a 300x speed-up on analytical workloads.

title: Cloudflare Built a Browser for Agents Instead of People
summary: Cloudflare released Kitesurf, a browser designed to be driven by AI agents rather than displayed to a human.

title: An AI Agent Broke Into Hugging Face by Accident
summary: Hugging Face — the site where most open AI models are hosted and downloaded — published a technical timeline of a July incident in which an automated agent belonging to another AI lab got into its systems, alongside its formal security disclosure.

title: ChatGPT Will No Longer Copy a Named Author's Style
summary: OpenAI has started blocking direct requests to write in the voice of a specific named author.

title: Danish Students Will Have to Defend Their Essays Out Loud
summary: Denmark will require high schoolers to verbally defend written assignments, so the grade rests on whether the student can explain the work rather than on who or what typed it.

title: Fastmail Adds an EU Data Region
summary: Email provider Fastmail now lets customers keep their data stored inside the European Union.

title: NVIDIA Brings Real-Time Simulation to Surgical Robots
summary: NVIDIA released Cosmos-H-Dreams, a system that generates simulated surgical environments fast enough to run in real time.

title: Shopify Replaced Redis With MySQL — and It Scaled
summary: Shopify moved inventory reservations — the short-lived holds placed on stock while a shopper is checking out — out of Redis, an in-memory cache, and into MySQL, the relational database it already runs.

title: Case-Folding Every Byte of Code Search at Memory Speed
summary: GitHub described how its code search normalises upper and lower case across every byte it indexes.

title: Anthropic Releases Claude Opus 5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, an update to its Opus tier of models, available today.

title: A Japanese Court Overturned Red's RAW Video Patent
summary: Panasonic won a case in Japan invalidating Red's patent on compressed RAW video recording — a patent Apple, Sony and Nikon had all failed to overturn.

title: A Working Method for Learning Hard Things With an AI Model
summary: A developer wrote up the routine they use to learn unfamiliar technical subjects with a language model: not asking it for answers, but using it to test whether their own explanation holds up.

title: Windows 11's Weather App Uses More Than a Gigabyte of Memory
summary: Testing found the small weather widget built into Windows 11 holding over 1 GB of RAM — more than many full applications.

title: Turn Satellite Imagery Into a Paper Globe You Fold Yourself
summary: A small web tool takes satellite imagery and lays it out as a printable net you cut and fold into a globe.

title: 4-Bit Image Generation Lands in Diffusers
summary: Hugging Face added Nunchaku 4-bit inference to Diffusers, the standard Python library for running image-generation models.

title: Idle GPUs Are the New Grounded Aircraft
summary: A piece on GPU management argues that AI infrastructure should be measured the way airlines measure fleets: the expensive asset only earns while it is in use, so utilisation matters more than how many you own.

title: Meta Returns to Open Models With Muse Glimmer
summary: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter model that handles both text and images and is designed for always-on local agents — software that keeps running in the background on your machine.

title: An AI Model Small Enough for a Watch
summary: Cactus released Needle2, an agentic model of roughly 14 megabytes — small enough to sit inside a phone app, a smartwatch, or a home device.

title: The UK's Push Against Online Anonymity Is Arriving in the US
summary: A report traces how the lobbying that produced Britain's age-verification and online identity rules is now working on American legislatures.

title: One Open Voice Model, Twelve Languages
summary: NVIDIA published Magpie TTS with open weights: a text-to-speech model built for real-time conversation in twelve languages, which you can run on your own hardware instead of paying per request to a service.

title: Sonic Pi, the Code-Your-Own-Music Tool, Reaches Version 5
summary: Sonic Pi, free software widely used in classrooms to teach programming by making music, shipped version 5.

title: Making Model Shrinking Cheap Enough to Do Routinely
summary: Multiverse Computing described two systems changes that bring down the cost of knowledge distillation — training a small 'student' model to reproduce the behaviour of a larger 'teacher'.

title: GitHub Ships a Copilot SDK for Java
summary: GitHub released a Java SDK for Copilot, so a Java application can drive the model from ordinary Java code — using annotations to declare what the model may call, and virtual threads to run many requests at once — instead of shelling out to a command-line tool or hand-writing HTTP calls.

title: London Underground Starts Scanning Passengers' Faces
summary: British Transport Police are expanding their live facial recognition trial into London Underground stations, where cameras check passing faces against a watchlist in real time.

title: A Firm Selling "100% Human-Written" Research Was Using AI for All of It
summary: 404 Media reports that a company marketing medical research and peer review as never AI-generated was in fact producing it entirely with AI.

title: An Officer Is Accused of Using a Camera Network to Follow an Ex-Partner
summary: A New Bedford police officer allegedly used Flock's automated licence plate camera network to track a former romantic partner.

title: Researchers Test Whether AI Models Can Notice Their Own Thinking
summary: A new paper looks at whether large language models can accurately report what is happening inside them, or whether they just produce a plausible-sounding story about it.

title: Mojo, the Python-Like Language Built for AI, Reaches 1.0
summary: Modular shipped version 1.

title: Two Ways to Let an Agent Learn From Itself — and What Each Costs in Tokens
summary: IBM Research compared its ALTK-Evolve approach with ACE.

title: Postgres Hands Analytics Queries Off to ClickHouse
summary: pg_clickhouse v0.

title: Three New AI Models Landed on the Same Day
summary: DeepSeek published V4 Pro, Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.

title: uBlock Origin Stops Trying to Block Facebook Ads
summary: uBlock Origin, the most widely used ad blocker, is giving up on keeping ads off Facebook.

title: Someone Is Scanning the Web While Pretending to Be an AI Bot
summary: A report describes mass scans hunting for security holes across websites, disguised so the traffic looks like well-known AI crawlers such as ClaudeBot.

title: Open Source Projects Are Getting AI-Written Contributions Whether They Want Them or Not
summary: A maintainer of AutoGPT, writing on GitHub's blog, says AI-generated contributions are already arriving in project queues and shares the written rules and review gates they use to stay in control of what gets accepted.

title: The Developer Job Is Drifting From Writing to Directing
summary: GitHub argues that as AI agents take on more of the typing, developers are increasingly responsible for the whole delivery system around the code rather than the code itself.

title: Tailscale Traced Data Corruption to a 16-Year-Old SQLite Bug
summary: Tailscale investigated databases that were coming back damaged and traced the cause to a bug in SQLite's write-ahead log reset — the mechanism that lets a database record changes to a side file first and fold them back into the main file later.

title: A Vision Model Small Enough to Run on Your Own Machine
summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.

title: 1,200 Volunteers Tried to Reproduce 2,200 AI Papers
summary: Hugging Face ran a three-week community hackathon in which more than 1,200 people took papers from ICML, one of the field's biggest machine learning conferences, and tried to re-run the work themselves.

title: Google Releases Gemini 3.7 Flash
summary: Google published Gemini 3.

title: Someone Followed 657,607 Links to See How Much of the Web Is Gone
summary: A researcher traced 657,607 links to find out how many still lead anywhere.

title: The US Government Ran a Mass Surveillance Campaign Against Protesters
summary: The Guardian reports that US authorities carried out broad digital spying on left-wing and anti-ICE protesters.

title: Mistral Updates Its Document-Reading Model
summary: Mistral shipped OCR 4.

title: One Log Line, 110 Kilobytes of Disk Writes
summary: A bug report against systemd — the software that starts and supervises services on most Linux servers — shows that writing a single line to the system log can trigger 49 KB or more of actual disk writes on the ext4 filesystem, and 110 KB or more on btrfs.

title: Breaking a Giant AI-Written Pull Request Into Reviewable Pieces
summary: GitHub published a method for stopping coding agents from dumping one enormous change into review.

title: Google Is Making AI That Works on Data It Cannot Read
summary: Google published how it is using homomorphic encryption — a method that lets a computer run calculations on encrypted data without ever unlocking it — to make private AI features practical in real products rather than just in research papers.

title: Where Open AI Models Actually Stand This Summer
summary: Hugging Face published its half-yearly review of open models — the ones anyone can download and run on their own machines.

title: Firefox Is Now the Last Major Browser Where uBlock Origin Still Works
summary: Chrome and the other Chromium-based browsers have finished phasing out the extension format uBlock Origin depends on, leaving Firefox as the only major browser where the ad blocker still runs in full.

title: A New Open Coding Model Arrives With Security Skills Attached
summary: Z.

title: What 50 Open Source Projects Learned About Security in the AI Era
summary: GitHub wrote up the fourth round of its Secure Open Source Fund, where 50 projects combined AI-assisted workflows, maintainer expertise, security tooling and funding to harden their code.

title: One Loop From Robot Demonstration to Deployed Policy
summary: Amazon and Hugging Face described a single pipeline for training robots: record a human demonstration straight into a cloud storage bucket, store it with byte-level deduplication so repeated frames are not saved twice, train by streaming the data from the Hub instead of downloading a copy, then deploy the resulting policy and feed its new recordings back into the same loop.

title: RustDesk Adds Unattended Remote Access on Wayland
summary: RustDesk, the open source alternative to TeamViewer, now supports true unattended remote access on Wayland — the display system that has been replacing the decades-old X11 on Linux desktops.
